operations.name: Saw Cut Tube Blank
operations.setup_note: Support the tube in soft-lined V-blocks and cut individual blanks with allowance for facing both ends. Verify the incoming bore permits complete cleanup within the finished bore limits before releasing the lot to machining.

operations.name: CNC Turn – First End
operations.setup_note: Grip the rear stock band in bored, full-wrap soft jaws at validated low pressure, using the first faced end as a process axial reference rather than a drawing datum. Rough the exposed OD, finish the through bore to establish datum A, then finish the exposed OD and first end chamfer without unloading.

operations.name: CNC Turn – Second End
operations.setup_note: Reverse the component onto a low-expansion, full-contact bore mandrel aligned to datum A, with the finished first face against an axial process stop. Face to final length, rough and finish only the remaining rear OD band with a controlled blend into the first setup's surface, and cut the second end chamfer.

operations.name: Production Deburr and Clean
operations.setup_note: Support the ring without squeezing its thin wall and rapidly remove residual burrs, applying the general 0.5 mm maximum break only to otherwise unspecified sharp edges. Clean away chips and cutting-fluid residue using an approved aluminum-compatible method, preserving the detailed end chamfers.

operations.name: Shop-Floor Quality Release
operations.setup_note: Inspect thermally stabilized SPC samples using dedicated bore and length gauges, a validated bore-referenced positional gauge honoring datum A's maximum-material boundary, and low-force OD gauging. Verify the AVG diameter and circularity using the approved free-state method, with clean handling before release to blasting.

operations.name: Media Blast – Immediate Bond-Prep Handoff
operations.setup_note: At the confirmed downstream bond-preparation facility, support the released rings without distortion and media blast per the controlled PS-175.1 specification. Process fixture-sized batches from the 100-piece order and hand each batch immediately to bond preparation, without intervening storage, shipment, or dimensional inspection.

clarifications.question: Can the proposed 80 mm OD × 72.01 mm nominal ID tube be supplied with guaranteed complete bore cleanup within the finished 71.88–72.14 mm diameter limits?
clarifications.suggested_default: Treat the tube dimensions as provisional and release stock only after cleanup capability is verified; if unsuitable, revise procurement to smaller-ID tube and reassess boring stock removal.

clarifications.question: Does Detail X's 2 mm edge-break width run axially along the outer cylindrical surface?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use the permitted chamfer interpretation with 2 mm axial width and 0.75 mm radial height, respecting the individual limits.

clarifications.question: Please provide the controlled PS-175.1 specification applicable to this drawing.
Which facility owns the bond-preparation step that must immediately follow media blasting?
clarifications.suggested_default: Perform blasting at the downstream bonding facility and hand parts directly into its bond-preparation process; do not ship or store parts after blasting.

assumptions.text: The front-view Z axis is the common physical cylinder axis; Section A-A axial X labels are view-local. Datum A establishes only the bore axis, while faced surfaces provide unnamed process axial references.
The material is supplied in the specified T6 condition. No additional heat treatment is required, HRC is not inferred for aluminum, and all route operations retain easy machinability.

Thin-wall geometry favors tube rather than solid bar, and quantity 100 does not justify forging. An 80 mm nominal OD tube is provisionally assumed available; its 72.01 mm nominal ID follows the bore feature and requires procurement confirmation. The 0.5 mm machining allowance applies to intermediate OD finishing stock, not to every surface.

The provisional tube bore needs only a light finish-boring cut, so separate rough boring is omitted. The finished bore may be aimed above the incoming nominal ID while remaining within the drawing limits; complete cleanup must be demonstrated before machining release.

The two mandatory lathe setups consolidate each accessible end's facing, canned OD roughing/finishing, and chamfering. Each OD cycle removes stock only from its assigned axial region, not repeatedly from the full raw-stock envelope; bore finishing precedes OD finishing, and low-pressure workholding must be qualified against free-state distortion.

F01 is produced as the drawing-permitted chamfer at both ends, provisionally interpreting its width as axial and height as radial. Its detailed limits override the general 0.5 mm maximum edge-break note, and no 45-degree chamfer is assumed.

Turning-template center drilling and tailstock support are omitted because this is a short, already hollow ring. Grooving and threading are omitted because no such features exist; parting is omitted because blanks are individually sawn, with both sawn ends subsequently faced.

The hole-making sequence is represented by finish boring and the shared final deburr gate. Spotting, pilot/full/peck drilling, reaming, tapping, countersinking, counterboring, and spotfacing are omitted because the tube supplies the through opening and no corresponding features or H7-class requirements exist; honing and grinding are unnecessary.
The pre-loaded milling sequence and conditional VMC consolidation correction are not applicable: the graph has no flats, slots, cross-holes, pockets, or other prismatic machining features.

Media blasting is the only specified surface treatment and is mapped to shot_blast without selecting an unprovided abrasive. All machining, deburring, cleaning, and dimensional release precede it; coating deposition, curing, hydrogen-relief baking, coating-thickness allowances, and coating-specific tests are omitted. Masking and unmasking are provisionally omitted pending PS-175.1 requirements.

The route ends at the controlled handoff from blasting to downstream bond preparation. Bond preparation, adhesive application, and assembly are not independently routed because their scope and specifications are absent; the downstream facility must maintain immediate sequencing and validate that blasting preserves dimensional acceptance.

Bench finishing is rapid production deburr/clean rather than prolonged hand finishing. Inspection uses dedicated gauges and SPC sampling rather than 100% CMM layout; the organizational bench and inspection cycle caps apply in Pass 2. No crush or functional test is added because none is specified.

Sawing, general-note deburring, cleaning, inspection, and media blasting carry empty target lists because they do not create a separately identified finished geometric feature. F03 and F01 are count-two groups, with one end instance produced in each lathe setup; F02 is an exempt part-body feature.
